messages:
mina: Heads up — just ran the OORT customer LoRA merge on our int4 quantized build and the structured extraction pipeline lost the 'order_id' field in ~16% of responses. FP16 baseline looks fine. Anyone seen field dropouts like this after quantizing a LoRA merge?
ryan: ugh that's bad. quick question — is this on Hosted or Dedicated?
mina: Dedicated (eu-west dedicated pool, q8_0->int4 pipeline). Repro deck attached in the quick eval run (120 prompts, mix of JSON-structured responses + free text).
devon: can you paste an example mismatch? small snippet is fine.
mina: sure — FP16: {
  "order_id": "ORD-9082",
  "amount": 42.50
}
int4: {
  "amount": 42.50
}
ryan: so order_id key is missing entirely, not just tokenized differently. interesting.
sam: tagging runtime team — @henry any kernel/kv-cache heuristics that could drop short prefixes when merging adapters?
henry: I haven't seen structural keys vanish before. two quick guesses: (1) tokenizer changes between checkpoints (special tokens split) causing the model to emit slightly different structure, or (2) kvcache/prerun truncation with aggressive batching + prefix caching.
devon: can you repro with kvcache disabled? also try setting "preserve_special_tokens": true in the serving config for that model variant.
mina: running kvcache=false now on a small set, will report.
mina: also ran the quick eval metrics — EM on order_id dropped from 98.2% (fp16) to 82.1% (int4). Other slots like amount/name unaffected.
ryan: that suggests it's not generic hallucination, more like tokenization or truncation of a short symbol-heavy field. any locale/currency tokens in order_id?
mina: order_id format is alphanumeric with dashes (ORD-XXXX). No weird unicode.
sam: can you dump the tokenization for a failing example (both fp16 and int4 outputs)? e.g., run: 
```
python infra/tools/tokenize_display.py --model oort-lora-merged:fp16 --text "ORD-9082"
python infra/tools/tokenize_display.py --model oort-lora-merged:int4 --text "ORD-9082"
```
post the token lists.
henry: also check model config for different bos/eos or postprocessors between variants. and confirm runtime used the same tokenizer binary — sometimes packaging picks a different tokenizer from the LOCALED model dir.
mina: token dumps: fp16 -> ["ORD", "-", "9082"] ; int4 -> ["ORD", "-", "90", "82"]
mina: int4 tokenization still reconstructs the string when joined, so tokenization not the cause.
devon: then likely early-stop or trimming — does the serving runtime apply a max_response_tokens per client route? maybe integer overflow in continuous batching?
ryan: check the logs for truncated responses in the inference trace. run with TRACE=gen to capture token stream.
mina: ran trace (attached). found a few instances where stream closed with status code 200 but finalization step didn't include the last few tokens — kvcache flush timestamp aligned with batch commit.
henry: ok that points to kvcache + batching interplay. we had a small bug in the int4 runner where the final writeback could drop trailing short sequences when batch_size > 8 and kv_flush_on_batch=true. patch landed in runtime branch but not on dedicated pool image.
sam: recommended immediate mitigation: 1) redeploy dedicated pool image with runtime patch; 2) in the meantime, set kvcache=false for that customer route or set batch_size to 1.
mina: testing kvcache=false on 100 prompts now, initial pass shows EM recovered to 97.9% (close to fp16).
devon: great — please capture a small evalpack with the failing prompts (labelled) and push to the customer folder so we can run regression tests post patch. Also add a quick CI check: run oort-lora-merged:int4 vs fp16 exact-match on order_id with threshold 95%.
mina: will do. created evalpack: /evalpacks/customer-oort/order-id-smoke-2026-03-23.json (120 prompts, flagged 20 failing cases).
mina: also notifying account team that we have a temporary mitigation and a fix will be rolled to Dedicated images in next patch.
deploy-bot: Deploy started for runtime/fix-int4-kvflush to dedicated-eu-west (canary) — build 2026.03.23-42.
ryan: once canary is healthy, let's run the full evalpack automatically and confirm EM >= 95% before rolling.
henry: I'll monitor the canary logs and post results here.
mina: thanks all — update in ~30m after canary run. :thumbsup:
